# #001 performance notes

## 29 Sep 2026: first 2 days (published 27 Sep, auto-generated thumbnail, no pinned comment)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Views | 26 (13 on each day) |
| Watch time | 2.59 h |
| Average view duration | ~6:00 (48% of 12:28), derived from watch time ÷ views |
| Impressions | 531 |
| Impressions CTR | 1.69% (≈ 9 views came from impressions) |
| Subscribers | 0 |

What it suggests, with only 26 views behind it:

- **Retention is the good news.** Viewers who start watch about half the video. For a 12-minute documentary, anything above 35–40% is healthy. So the script and visuals are holding people, and that is the metric that is hardest to fix later.
- **Click-through rate is the problem, as expected.** 1.69% is low, but it was measured on an auto-selected frame, which on this video is a dark underwater or storm shot. The custom thumbnails are the fix.
- ~~About 17 of the 26 views didn't come from impressions (direct, external or channel page).~~ **Wrong, corrected below:** 20 of the 26 views came from Suggested, and most of the ones that weren't clicks were autoplay.

Actions taken or recommended:

1. Upload `thumb-a.jpg` and start Test & Compare with A, B and C.
2. Post and pin the pinned comment from `package.md`.
3. For the 7-day review, export Traffic source (with impressions and CTR per source) and screenshot the audience retention curve. This export only had the summary table.

## 29 Sep 2026: traffic sources and retention (Studio screenshots + export)

| Source | Views | Avg view duration | Impressions | CTR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Suggested videos | 20 | 7:25 (60%) | 528 | 1.7% |
| External (Facebook) | 3 | 1:44 | – | – |
| Browse | 2 | 0:45 | 1 | – |
| Other YouTube features | 1 | 0:46 | – | – |
| Search | 0 | – | 2 | 0% |

- **YouTube is doing the distributing.** 99.6% of impressions come from recommendations, placed next to history and mystery videos (Taos Hum, "Ancient Mexico with AI", DVD history, Mandela-effect/CERN). Search hasn't started yet.
- **Of 20 Suggested views, only ~9 were thumbnail clicks; the other ~11 were autoplay.** Autoplay viewers stayed: 7:25 average.
- **The funnel's "engaged views from impressions" (9 views, 5:19 average, 43%) is the cleanest signal.** These are strangers who chose to click, and they watched about 43%. That's good.
- **Caution:** 30 views from only 12 unique viewers, and 61% of watch time on TV. Some of the retention is likely autoplay on a TV and repeat plays. The Facebook shares averaged 1:44.
- **Retention curve (12 viewers, so each step ≈ one person):**
  - The biggest early drop is between ~0:40 and ~2:00. That spans the end of the cold open, the **3.5 s silent title card at 1:23** and the museum scene.
  - It is flat at ~57% from ~2:30 to ~9:15.
  - A second drop comes at ~9:15–9:45, in *The face of the cosmos*, as the planets and reconstruction section starts (the part that is hypothesis, not surviving evidence).
- **A/B test:** the user is running three custom title + thumbnail pairs ("GREEK COMPUTER?", "PREDICTED ECLIPSES", "FOUND UNDERWATER"). Because titles and thumbnails vary together, the winner tells us which *pair* works, not which element. The result is due around 13 Oct.

**Carry into #002:**

- No silent title card. Put the title over narration, or drop it, and move straight from the cold open into the story.
- Keep sections built on reconstruction short, and bring back a concrete surviving object or number within ~30 s.
- The recommendation neighbours suggest a curious history/mystery audience. Titles can lean toward mystery ("the clock that…") as long as the video pays it off.
